newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ mid bonds bought from offshore ahead of key CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ mid bonds bought from offshore ahead of key CPI.

text.p: New Zealand mid bonds rallied sharply at Tuesday's open on the back of bidding interest from an offshore player in the 02/01 maturity ahead of key inflation data due at 2245 GMT.

The 02/01 bond yield was down a substantial 10 basis points to 8.04 percent, while the 02/00s rallied eight to 7.97 percent, sharply outperforming U.S. three-year bonds by narrowing the spread nine points to 143 over.

Short bonds rallied two to three basis points, while from the 03/02s to the long end of the curve, bonds were down four to five basis points in yield. Trade had quietened by early morning but the market still had a tentative bid, helped by a NZ$100 million 05/02 Eurobond issued by a Commerzbank unit overnight.
Dealers said the offshore buying in the 01s had been worth less than NZ$100 million but it was still a sizeable chunk, and had hit a relatively thin market at the same time as the Eurokiwi.
Dealers said it was possible the offshore buyer was taking a position on an expectation of CPI data in line with forecasts.
The market has grown increasingly bullish over the prospects of March quarter underlying inflation at or below Reserve Bank of New Zealand expectations of 0.5 percent.
The RBNZ expects 2.2 percent annual core inflation, well down from 2.6 percent in the year to December.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average expectation of 0.41 percent quarterly underlying inflation, for 2.16 percent annually.

Dealers have speculated that if the data prove benign and the market does not ease monetary conditions to the RBNZ's liking, the central bank may step in to ease them further through a public comment.
A Wellington dealer said he was nervous ahead of the CPI and saw strong selling if the market did not get the tame data it expected. December's numbers had been surprisingly strong.

If the March quarter figures also surprised on the upside and the long end of the yield curve stayed at current levels, the curve could flatten by 10 basis points, the dealer said. He suggested the 02/01s could retrace to around 8.20 percent.

"The key for the day... is whether the Reserve Bank is going to come out and say something. Everyone is waiting for this to happen, and if it doesn't happen we could be off to the races on the selling."

Meanwhile, the money market opened a fraction stronger. Dealers said most traders had positioned themselves for the data and were twiddling their thumbs waiting for 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT) to roll around.

They said they would be keeping a close eye on the reaction of the currency to the data, as a strong number would leave the Kiwi well bid. Monetary conditions would then remain stronger than the RBNZ desired, limiting the ability of short rates to sell off too far. --------------------------(SPREADS)----------------------------- NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD
